buttonTooltip: Check this lesson against the lesson standard
title: Check lesson
description: These follow the same rules an AI assistant is held to. Nothing here stops you saving or exporting.
empty: Nothing to check yet. Add a section to get started.
problemsHint: Things that would confuse the speller or mark a right answer wrong.
suggestionsHint: The usual shape of a lesson. Ignore these if you meant to do it differently.

codes.E_GROUNDING_SINGLE: Question {{question}}: the answer "{{answer}}" isn't in this section's passage. A single answer question needs its answer written word for word in the text.
codes.E_GROUNDING_MULTIPLE: Question {{question}}: the answer "{{answer}}" isn't in this section's passage. Use the passage's own wording.
codes.E_ORANGE_PARAPHRASED: Question {{question}}: "{{answer}}" isn't a word the passage uses. A multiple answers question asks for items the passage lists, so its answers have to match the text. If you want the speller to answer in their own words (a synonym, say), make it a suggested answers question.
codes.E_ORANGE_ANSWER_IN_PROMPT_one: Question {{question}}: the question itself says {{answers}}, which is one of its own answers, so there is nothing left to recall. Blank the list out of the quoted sentence with ______ instead.
codes.E_ORANGE_ANSWER_IN_PROMPT_other: Question {{question}}: the question itself says {{answers}}, which are its own answers, so there is nothing left to recall. Blank the list out of the quoted sentence with ______ instead.
codes.E_ORANGE_NOT_A_LIST: Question {{question}}: {{answers}} are all in the passage, but not together as one list. Write them into a sentence as a series ("rock, gas, and ash"), or make this a suggested answers question.
codes.E_ORANGE_PARTIAL_LIST: Question {{question}}: the passage's list goes on to "{{next}}", which this question doesn't accept. A speller who names it would be marked wrong. Add it to the answers, or take it out of the list in the passage.
codes.E_GROUNDING_NUMBER_FILL: Question {{question}}: {{answer}} isn't in this section's passage. A fill in the blank number question needs the number in the text. If this is the word problem, add its worked steps.
codes.E_ANSWER_REVEALED_CROSS: Question {{question}} names {{leaks}}, so the speller can copy it across instead of recalling it. Reword it.
codes.E_BACKGROUND_IN_TEXT: Question {{question}}: "{{answer}}" is in the passage, so this background knowledge question isn't asking for anything from outside the lesson. Ask about something the passage doesn't say, or make it a single answer question.
codes.E_BACKGROUND_NO_CONTEXT: Question {{question}}: this background knowledge question has no background note. Add what the speller is expected to already know.
codes.E_SPELLING_LENGTH: "{{word}}" is {{letters}} letters long. Spelling words should be {{min}} to {{max}} letters.
codes.E_SPELLING_DUPLICATE: "{{word}}" is also a spelling word in section {{otherSection}}. Each section needs its own words.
codes.E_SPELLING_COLLISION: The spelling word "{{word}}" appears inside "{{answer}}", the answer to {{other}}. The warm up would give that answer away.
codes.E_ANSWER_WORD_REUSED: Question {{question}}: "{{answer}}" is also the answer to {{other}}. Give each question its own answer word.
codes.E_ANSWER_WORD_REUSED_inside: Question {{question}}: "{{answer}}" also turns up inside "{{otherAnswer}}", the answer to {{other}}. Give each question its own answer word.
codes.E_NUMBER_DUPLICATE: Question {{question}}: {{answer}} is also the answer to {{other}}. Give each number question a different answer.
codes.E_RETIRED_STEM: Question {{question}}: "a word that comes to mind" has been used so much it's become a habit. Name an everyday category instead, like "Name something found in a hospital".
codes.E_FORMAT_HEAVY_one: Too much of this section's text is formatted. Keep passages plain, since capitals already mark the vocabulary. Format only what a convention calls for, like a book's title.
codes.E_FORMAT_HEAVY_other: This section's text has {{count}} formatted phrases. Keep passages plain, since capitals already mark the vocabulary. Format only what a convention calls for, like a book's title, and no more than {{max}} per section.
codes.E_FORMAT_LONG_EMPHASIS: "{{text}}" is underlined across {{words}} words. Write it plain and let the wording carry the weight.
codes.E_FORMAT_LONG_EMPHASIS_bold: "{{text}}" is bold across {{words}} words. Write it plain and let the wording carry the weight.
codes.E_FORMAT_LONG_ITALIC: "{{text}}" is in italics across {{words}} words. Italics are for a title or a term, not a sentence.
codes.E_UNKNOWN_SOURCE: A footnote cites "@{{sourceId}}", which isn't one of this lesson's sources. Add the source, or fix the footnote.
codes.W_SECTION_COUNT_one: This lesson has {{count}} section. The usual length is {{expected}}.
codes.W_SECTION_COUNT_other: This lesson has {{count}} sections. The usual length is {{expected}}.
codes.W_QUESTION_SHAPE: The questions aren't in the usual order: 3 single answer, 2 number answer, 2 multiple or suggested answers, 1 background knowledge, then 7 open ended.
codes.W_NO_QUESTION: This section has no questions yet.
codes.W_OPEN_SPLIT: The open ended questions don't read as {{tight}} quick ones followed by {{extended}} longer ones. The first {{tight}} usually take a one word answer ("Name something found in a hospital"), and the last {{extended}} a full sentence ("In your own words, explain why").
codes.W_ORANGE_MULTIWORD: Question {{question}}: "{{answer}}" is more than one word. The speller has to spell every word on the letterboard.
codes.W_ORANGE_ANSWER_COUNT_one: Question {{question}} accepts {{count}} answer. Aim for {{min}} to {{max}}, so the speller has a real choice.
codes.W_ORANGE_ANSWER_COUNT_other: Question {{question}} accepts {{count}} answers. Aim for {{min}} to {{max}}, so the speller has a real choice.
codes.W_ORANGE_ANSWER_COUNT_open: Question {{question}} has no suggested answers. Add at least one so whoever is scoring knows what would count.
codes.W_ORANGE_NO_BLANK: Question {{question}} doesn't show which list it's asking for. Quote the passage's sentence with the list blanked out: "The blast sent out ______."
codes.W_ORANGE_ORDER: A suggested answers question comes before a multiple answers one. The multiple answers question usually goes first.
codes.W_SPELLING_COUNT_one: This section has {{count}} spelling word. The usual number is {{expected}}.
codes.W_SPELLING_COUNT_other: This section has {{count}} spelling words. The usual number is {{expected}}.
codes.W_NUMBER_NO_STEPS: Neither number answer question has worked steps. The second one is usually the word problem, so add its steps.
codes.W_SPELLING_IN_CAPS: "{{word}}" is also capitalised vocabulary in the passage. Pick a different spelling word on the same theme.
codes.W_ANSWER_REVEALED_OPEN: Question {{question}} names {{leaks}}. That's fine if the question is about that word. Otherwise, reword it.
codes.W_WYR_SHAPE: Question {{question}} doesn't read as a choice. Start with "Would you rather" and join two options with "or".
codes.W_WYR_SHAPE_many: Question {{question}} strings together {{ors}} uses of "or". Offer two options, or a short list joined by one "or".
codes.W_FORMAT_BOLD: This section uses bold ({{spans}}). Capitals already mark the vocabulary, so bold is rarely needed.
codes.W_FORMAT_UNDERLINE: This section uses underlining ({{spans}}). On screen it looks like a link that goes nowhere.
codes.W_FORMAT_CAPS: This section formats capitalised vocabulary ({{spans}}). The capitals already mark it.
codes.W_VAKT_NOT_LAST: The VAKT activity isn't at the end of the section. It usually goes after the questions.
